title: Mission: type it, then move it
drDigitalIntro:
Copying between two different programs is the moment typing stops being typing and starts being useful.
• You will type a sentence in one of your own apps, copy it, and paste it into the box on this page.
• The box can tell the difference between text you typed and text you pasted, so it only counts if the copy really worked.
• The sentence to type is: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
• It uses every letter of the alphabet, which is why typists have practised on it for a hundred years.

playgroundTask.goal: You typed it, copied it and pasted it between two real programs

steps.say: Open something you can type in on your own computer.
steps.detail: A notes app, an email you never send, even the search box in another window. Anywhere text can go.

steps.say: Type this into it: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
steps.detail: Capital T at the start, full stop at the end. Take your time — accuracy first, speed comes later and comes free.

steps.say: Select it, copy it, and paste it into the box below.
steps.detail: Select by dragging across the words. Copy with Ctrl+C, or Command+C on a Mac. Then click in the box below and press Ctrl+V, or Command+V.

steps.say: With that box active, press Ctrl+A (or Command+A) to select everything in it.
steps.detail: A is for all. It is the fastest way to grab a whole page of text without dragging across it.

steps.say: Back in your own app, undo what you typed with Ctrl+Z (or Command+Z).
steps.detail: Undo is the reason nothing you do to text is permanent. Press it more than once and it keeps stepping backwards.

drDigitalSuccess: You moved text out of one program and into another. That works between any two programs on the machine.
drDigitalHint: The box below only accepts text that arrives by pasting. If you type into it, nothing happens — copy from your own app instead.
